pm_exper_user_3615_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: How can I handle the frustration and helplessness I feel when a close friend is unfairly penalized by a teacher’s bias, and I can’t change the outcome for them?
pm_exper_user_3615_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) I know how painful it is to watch someone you care about be treated unfairly. While you can’t change what has happened, you can support them by listening without judgment, helping them regain confidence, and encouraging them to seek out environments where they are respected and valued.
(b) I know how disheartening it is to see a young creative friend face rejection from a prestigious art residency due to subtle discrimination. You may not be able to change the selection committee’s choice, but you can help them channel that pain into their work, remind them of the spaces that have embraced their artistry, and introduce them to curators and circles that will uplift them.
(c) I know how deeply it cuts to witness someone you’ve mentored face unjust treatment, especially when it echoes the same biases we’ve fought to dismantle. While you may not be able to reverse the teacher’s decision, you can help your friend reframe the setback as part of a longer journey, remind them of their worth, and connect them with spaces and allies where their identity is valued and celebrated.
(d) I know how frustrating it is to see someone you’ve mentored struggle with networking setbacks in their startup, especially when you’ve invested time and guidance in their vision. Even if you can’t undo a lost investor meeting, you can help them see it as one chapter in a much larger growth story, reaffirm their potential, and open doors to new supporters who believe in their ideas.
